definition: Firm honesty and moral uprightness, especially when trusted with money or public duties.
example: The scholar's probity showed when she published data that undercut her own theory.
nuance: Probity is honesty proven under trust or temptation; propriety means correct manners and behavior, not moral uprightness.
prompt: A town treasurer is retiring after thirty years of handling public funds.
options: No one ever doubted her probity; every dollar was accounted for.
Her probity showed when she quietly moved town funds into her own account.
The auditors' probity into her old ledgers took six weeks to finish.
There is a high probity that the council will hire her deputy next.
reasons: Spotless records kept over decades of trust show tested honesty.
Taking public money is dishonest, the reverse of what the word praises.
This confuses the word with probe; it names a quality, not an investigation.
This mistakes the word for probability; it has nothing to do with likelihood.

practice.prompt: A referee is assigned to officiate a championship game involving his former team.
options: The referee's probity led him to favor his former teammates on every close call.
With remarkable probity, the referee sprinted the whole length of the field in seconds.
The referee's probity was obvious from his neatly pressed uniform and polished shoes.
Known for his probity, the referee penalized his old team as readily as its rivals.
reasons: Biased calls are unfair, the opposite of the integrity the word describes.
Speed is a physical ability, not a sign of honesty or principle.
A tidy appearance says nothing about character; the word concerns ethics, not looks.
Refusing to play favorites despite personal ties shows moral uprightness.
